notes: Independent critic review of the current 24 Part A weather PNGs and seven requested reference PNGs. Read BRIEF-16 in full and the drawing-method sections of NOTES. No production artwork, references, existing GIFs, previous reviews, notes or scripts were edited. Visual inspection: every named PNG at native 1x and nearest-neighbour 4x; all four phases of every weather family in literal 3x3 weather repeats over all seven references; 3x seam-junction crops for every phase/reference; selected drawn particles at 8x, and isolated snow/sandstorm seams at 4x. The 42 critic-r16A-3-repeats-*.png sheets each contain four unscaled 576x576 repeat panels. Ground-reference boundaries every 288 px are repeated camera-crop boundaries, not 192 px weather seams. No remaining weather seam, conspicuous repeated curtain, rounded tile border, blur, fringe, accidental detached cleanup speck, oversized outline or unreadable map area was found. Rain has short east-leaning strokes and tiny ticks; heavy rain is visibly longer, darker and over twice as dense. Snow retains 2-3 px pale flakes with blue-grey edges visible on winter ground; the former broad curved curtains are no longer evident. Hail has compact hard facets and bounce marks, distinct from the broader cross-like snow flakes. Blizzard reads as a dense sideways blast with thinner wind strands while roads and settlements remain identifiable. Sandstorm now has varied thin fragments, open curls and broken patches rather than a sequence of identical crests; it stays tan/gold over grass and visible over sand, without muddy opaque masses or a fog sheet.
